comment: Every skip in this repository is runtime-conditional on a host or environment fact -- a CUDA device, an installed asset, an importable optional package -- so the skip count can move without anybody touching the code, and nothing recorded that it had. The coverage gate catches a test FILE that contributes nothing and validate_native_ci_exclusions.py catches a native SUITE that stops running; a collected file whose twenty tests all call pytest.skip() at runtime passes both. This file declares every reason a bound run may produce, and scripts/ci_skip_reason_gate.py reads a run's JUnit XML and fails on a reason that matches none of them. Reasons are anchored regular expressions rather than literals because several are f-strings and interpolate at the front, the middle and the end; the gate refuses a pattern that is not anchored, one that carries a wildcard behind fewer than 24 literal characters, and one that matches its canary strings, because a pattern that matches too much is the single failure that would make this whole gate decorative. Adding an entry here is the deliberate act: it costs one line and one stated reason, and it is the human glance the gate exists to force. This declaration carries no authority over what runs or what skips; the tests do.
scope: the non-GPU pytest runs listed under environments. The GPU job is deliberately NOT bound: two of its reasons are built at runtime from a device probe (`triton_status()[1]`, `receipt["reason"]` in tests/test_sm120_kernels.py), so their text is a property of the card in the machine rather than of the source, and pinning them would either churn per device or need a wildcard wide enough to defeat the check. It is also unreached today -- vars.TRAINVM_SELF_HOSTED is unset, recorded in docs/experiment-vm/gpu-grader-observations.v1.json -- so a pin there would be pinning nothing.

environments.name: github-hosted-cpu
environments.why: a hosted ubuntu-latest runner with a fixed install line and no accelerator, so its skip set is reproducible run to run and a count bound means something there

environments.name: github-hosted-fla
environments.why: the same hosted image with flash-linear-attention installed, running only the fla-marked selection; a skip here would mean the assertions this job exists to run stopped running

environments.name: real-host-acceptance
environments.why: the skip set on a real host is a function of that machine's devices, assets and optional packages, so a pinned count would be correct on one workstation and wrong on the next; a permanently red gate is one everybody learns to ignore, and the novel-reason half is enforced here regardless, which is the half worth having

reasons.pattern: ^trainvm gate binary not built in this checkout \(PATH is deliberately not consulted\); build it with: .+$
reasons.why: the native gate binary is gitignored, so a checkout that has not built it cannot grade against it; the build command is interpolated into the reason

reasons.pattern: ^no trainvm binary in this checkout; enumeration ran without it$
reasons.why: the step-zero enumeration cross-check needs the native binary's lifecycle declarations to compare against

reasons.pattern: ^this trainvm binary does not publish lifecycle declarations$
reasons.why: an older binary predates the declarations the cross-check reads, and grading against it would compare with nothing
rosa_soft is an optional compiled extension that is not part of any install line here
flash-linear-attention is deliberately absent from the CPU job and installed only in the fla job, which is what makes that job's coverage real
the Mage-Flow layers live in a separate environment that is not installed alongside this package
torchao is an optional quantization dependency; the tail is the interpreter's own ImportError text, which varies by version
torch is installed in every job that runs these tests, so this firing at all is worth seeing; the tail is the interpreter's ImportError text
Pillow arrives with the vision extra, so this fires wherever that extra was not installed
the Mage-Flow attention backend is part of that separate environment

reasons.pattern: ^AO3 corpus or RWKV vocabulary is not present on this host$
reasons.why: the input-pipeline tests read a real corpus that exists only on the training workstation

reasons.pattern: ^host AO3 corpus or RWKV tokenizer is not available: .+$
reasons.why: the benchmark runner's corpus fixture names which of the two is missing, so the tail varies with the host

reasons.pattern: ^ztok's Python binding is not importable \(it lives in the ztok repository, not this checkout\); .+$
reasons.why: the ztok binding is built in another repository; the tail reports where the search looked
the vocabulary cross-check needs a ztok build to compare against, and names which resolution step failed

reasons.pattern: ^production Qwen assets are not installed on this test host$
reasons.why: the caption parity fixture hashes real production weights, which are not distributed with the repository
the post-training test needs a gloo process group, which some builds of torch do not carry

the gate-verdict test drives each gate and skips the ones whose input this job does not have; the gate name interpolates at the FRONT of the reason, which is why entries here are expressions rather than prefixes
the runtime-closure builder refuses an interpreter whose files are group- or world-writable, and names the offending path

reasons.pattern: ^the runtime closure is a Linux deployment artifact$
reasons.why: the sealed closure is a Linux deployment artifact and the test says so rather than asserting something false elsewhere
the accelerator-mask probe runs a child interpreter and reports its stderr tail when the module under test would not import there

reasons.pattern: ^needs \S+=1; this test deliberately runs a child WITHOUT the accelerator mask, which the rest of this module exists to forbid$
reasons.why: the one test that must run unmasked is opt-in twice over, and names the variable that authorizes it

reasons.pattern: ^no NVIDIA device files on this host$
reasons.why: the device-file assertions have nothing to assert against on a machine with no NVIDIA nodes

reasons.pattern: ^this is the explicitly authorized accelerator phase$
reasons.why: the mask assertions are inverted during the authorized GPU phase, so they stand down rather than fail there
tests/conftest.py marks every gpu-marked item skipped unless accelerator access was explicitly granted, so a caller that forgets the marker expression still gets a default-deny
